newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's King Sihanouk says not opposed to ASEAN.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's King Sihanouk says not opposed to ASEAN.

text.p: King Norodom Sihanouk is not opposed to Cambodia's entry into the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN), the royal palace said on Friday.
But the king, in documents released by the royal palace, said he fears the social and economic costs of joining the powerful regional bloc.

Earlier this month the king's son, co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh, was quoted as saying Sihanouk regarded ASEAN as a political and military alliance and had strong reservations about entering the group.
"I am certainly very old but not 'senile' to the point of believing that the calling of ASEAN is of a military nature. I know full well that this calling is of an economic order," the king said.
Cambodia has applied to become a full member of ASEAN. The seven current members agreed late last year that Cambodia, Laos and Burma could be admitted at the same time.
ASEAN diplomats in Phnom Penh said this week that they expect the three nations to join this year, possibly as early as July when the regional club celebrates its 30th anniversary.
ASEAN members are Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
